Notable planes

Review of the 2026-11-21 build on branch claude/notable-planes-feature-a4225e. The screens are the real SwiftUI views rendered in the iOS 26 simulator with sample planes. Nothing is merged, deployed or on a phone yet.

The idea

Some individual planes are worth more than their type. A Boeing 757 is uncommon. The 757 that carries the Golden State Warriors is a find. The server now knows which airframes are notable, and the app marks them before the catch, names them after it, and pays a bonus.

Your calls so far, as built:

  • Scope is "names plus working aircraft": six kinds, listed in the table below.
  • Before the catch the label shows a gold star and nothing else. Who it is stays hidden until the reveal.
  • A notable catch earns +50% of its base.
  • Private individuals' jets are named as the source lists them.

Total in the committed snapshot5,138

This will be rare. Of 13,433 airframes players have caught since 2026-06-26, about 141 are in scope, covering about 205 of 28,324 catches (0.7%). Both figures were measured before the last changes to the rules, so treat them as approximate.

The live label

A notable plane gets a small gold star at the front of its label. There is no name and no category. VoiceOver says "Notable plane" and no more. Nothing in the app points you toward a notable plane elsewhere in the sky.

The four labels are the label's four styles: chosen, quiet, faint and pinned. The star was also checked on a dusk sky.

The reveal

The reveal is where the plane is named. A gold plate sits under the callsign line with the category and, when the source has one, the name. The points ledger gains a gold NOTABLE PLANE row and the total includes it.

  • When the source names nobody, the plate shows the category alone. 822 of the 5,138 airframes have no name.
  • A long category wraps to two lines, and so does a long name. The tallest case is on the right: with a route and a first-of-type row as well, the card is slightly taller than a 393 × 852 screen and scrolls. This is one of the decisions below.
  • Catching the same notable plane again is a duplicate like any other. The plate shows and no points are paid.

Multi-catch summary

Each notable plane in a multi-catch gets a star on its row, and the summary adds one NOTABLE PLANE row for the press.

The settled card

The card you see when you open a catch from the Hangar carries the same plate and the same ledger row.

Share cards

All three share formats show the plate. The photo gives up the height. The points on the card include the bonus.

The card back

The back of the card is about the type. It gains one line about this exact plane: a gold star and NOTABLE on the left, the name on the right, or the category when there is no name.

The Hangar

The row

A notable row leads with a solid gold star and has a gold line of its own under the callsign with the name, or the category when there is no name. That makes a notable row one line taller than the others. The first-of-type mark is a ringed sparkle on the model line, so a row with both shows two different marks.

The name line never wraps. A long name is cut with an ellipsis.

The Catches list and the Notable chip

The search field in the Catches list gains a gold Notable chip at its right end. Tap it and the list shows notable planes only. Tap it again to go back.

  • The chip appears only once the Hangar holds a notable plane. Until then the search field looks as it does today.
  • With the chip in place the hint in the field shortens from "Search callsign, airline, aircraft, tier" to "Search catches", because the long hint would be cut beside the chip.
  • Typing the word "notable" does the same as the chip, the way a tier name does.
  • Names and categories are searchable: "warriors" or "team plane" finds the row.
  • When nothing matches, the list says "No notable planes caught yet" or "No notable catches match" with the search text.

Trophies

A new track, Notables, with two levels, and one feat.

TrophyKindEarned by
Star SightingNotables track, level 1Catch a notable plane
Who's WhoNotables track, level 2Catch 10 different notable planes
Four of a KindFeat, visibleCatch notable planes of four different kinds

Planes are counted by airframe, so catching one team plane ten times counts once.

Past catches

  • On the first foreground after the update, the app lists your catches from the server once and marks the ones the server says are notable. Stars, name lines and the chip then appear in the Hangar, and any Notables trophy you have already earned unlocks right away.
  • The backfill only touches the three notable fields. It sets the mark when the server says a catch is notable and clears it when the server says it is not. It never deletes a catch and never touches another field.
  • It runs until one pass has read the whole list, then never again. If there is no network or no account yet, it tries again on the next foreground.
  • A Hangar restored on a new phone gets the marks as part of the restore.
  • Points for past catches come from a one-time re-score on the server, the same way the multi-catch bonus was paid.

Scoring

Scoring version 11. A notable catch earns +50% of its base, rounded. It adds to the base like first-of-type, the guess bonuses and the multi-catch bonus. Bonuses stack and never multiply each other.

TierBaseNotable planeTotalWith first of type too
Common10+51520
Uncommon20+103040
Rare50+2575100
Epic100+50150200
Legendary500+2507501,000
  • The server decides. It looks the plane up by its ICAO hex each time it scores, so nothing new is stored on a catch and there is no database migration.
  • Because of that, builds already on people's phones earn the bonus as soon as the server is deployed and re-scored. They show no star, plate or ledger row until they update.
  • If the source later adds a plane someone already caught, the catch shows as notable straight away but keeps its old points until a full re-score (npm run rescore -- --all). The same full pass takes the bonus back from a plane the source has removed.

Data source and refresh

  • The list is plane-alert-db, a community-maintained list of about 17,000 airframes under the Open Database License 1.0. Settings gains a credit row, "Notable aircraft data: plane-alert-db contributors (ODbL)".
  • The server loads a committed snapshot at boot (5,138 airframes). Thirty seconds later, and every 24 hours, it fetches the list again and swaps it in. There is nothing to maintain by hand.
  • A fetch that fails keeps the data the server had. A fetch that yields fewer than half the snapshot's entries is rejected, which covers a cut-off download or a reorganised file.
  • Each source category maps to one of our six kinds through an allow-list. A category the source adds later is excluded until someone maps it, so the unattended refresh cannot put a new kind of plane in front of users.
  • Routine military, police and air-ambulance airframes are excluded. Military rows are kept only for government and head-of-state flights, historic aircraft and display teams.
  • The source's own tags and category names are jokes and editorial labels written for hobbyists. They never leave the server. A user sees one of our six labels and the operator's name.
  • A name is the source's operator field, capped at 60 characters. Placeholders such as "Private" are dropped, so those planes show the category alone.

Decisions for Noah

  1. The Notable chip is new chrome inside the Hangar search field. It appears only once you have a notable catch, and it shortens the search hint. The alternative is no chip: typing "notable" already works.
  2. Notable Hangar rows are one line taller. The name did not fit on the callsign line ("Golden State Warriors" was cut to "Golden..."). The alternative is the star alone on the row, with the name on the card.
  3. Four of a Kind is visible, not secret. The two Notables levels already tell players the category exists. It could be a secret feat instead.
  4. The tallest reveal scrolls. A notable plane with a route and a first-of-type row slightly exceeds one screen on a 393 × 852 phone. Options: accept the scroll, or tighten the card for this case.
  5. "Special mission" includes US Department of Justice surveillance aircraft. They are named as the source lists them, for example "Department Of Justice (DOJ)" and leasing-company names ending in "(DOJ)". Options: keep, show the category without the name, or drop the surveillance category.
  6. Several source categories were left out on judgement. Say if any should come in.
    Source categoryWhat it holdsWhy it is out
    Joe CoolA mixed bag; 55 of 264 rows are ordinary Cirrus Vision jetsThey would wear a "Historic and special" badge they have not earned
    Da Comrade, UkraineMostly Soviet-era freighters, tagged for sanctions and arms-embargo historyNot a "special" we want to label
    Jesus he Knows meChurch and televangelist aircraftNo kind fits without the label becoming a comment on them
    Watch Me FlyTraining fleetsLeft out; the rules record no further reason
    UAVDronesLeft out; the rules record no further reason

Two things seen in the data while writing this, for the same conversation. The source files company jets and people together under its oligarch category, so that whole category shows as Business jet. Its football category holds an owner's jet as well as club aircraft, so one "Team plane" is named for a person.

Deploy order

The server must go first. That keeps points and stars in agreement. An app that meets an older server does no harm: its backfill of past catches stays pending and tries again on the next launch.
